Let j0 be the nonnegative symmetric grounded graph kernel with Delta_out j0(.,y)=delta_xi-delta_y, and J0(x)=integral j0(x,y)dmu0(y). Grounded uniqueness yields h(x)-h(xi)=-integral j0(x,y)dMA(phi)(y)+J0(x) for x on Gamma0; in that integral the kernel is pulled back by r0. The first integral is nonnegative, so h(x)-h(xi)<=J0(x)<=B=||J0||_infty<=a*sup j0. Radial monotonicity gives sup_T h=max_Gamma0 h, since h is continuous on the compact curve and core. Thus sup_T h-B<=h(xi)<=sup_T h, uniformly over ALL genuine weighted FS scalars, independently of their carriers and arbitrary real weights. No positive atom at xi is needed for this direct bound.
